2027-01-10.title: First Sunday after Denho
readings: The burning bush: I AM WHO I AM
The Lord has comforted his people
Chosen in Christ before the foundation of the world
The call of the first disciples
2027-01-10.verse: Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.
theo: After his Baptism Jesus begins his public ministry in Galilee. Matthew sees Isaiah fulfilled: “the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light.” Jesus' first preaching is short: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.” His first action is to call people: by the Sea of Galilee he sees Simon and Andrew, James and John at work, and says, “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.” “Immediately they left their nets and followed him.”

The Old Testament readings show God calling people in the middle of ordinary work. Moses was keeping his father-in-law's sheep when he saw the bush that burned and was not consumed, and heard: “Remove the sandals from your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground.” God reveals his name, “I AM WHO I AM”, and sends Moses to free his people. Jacob too was a shepherd, and God blessed the work of his hands.

St Paul says that this call did not begin by the lake. God “chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love” (Ephesians 1:4). And Acts shows what the call produces: a community that “devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers” (Acts 2:42).

Denho is the season of the manifestation of Christ. He is manifested not only at the Jordan, but every time someone leaves their nets and follows him. Each of us is called: to holiness, to a vocation, to bring others to Christ.
conn: Moses with the flock, David with the sheep, the apostles with their nets: God calls people in the middle of daily work.
Matthew 4:16 fulfils Isaiah 9:1–2, read at Yaldo: the light born in Bethlehem now shines in Galilee.
Jeremiah 16:16 speaks of God sending “many fishermen”; Jesus turns fishermen into his messengers.
Acts 2:42–47 is the model of every parish: teaching, fellowship, Eucharist, prayer, sharing.
altar: The first Christians were faithful to “the breaking of bread”. The Holy Qurbono is where the call to follow Jesus is renewed each Sunday: we leave our nets for an hour and come to the One who calls us.
outline: Ask: what are the “nets” that keep us busy?
Jesus begins where people live and work.
Moses at the burning bush: God calls in ordinary places. Reverence before the holy.
Immediate response. What do I need to leave to follow him?
Acts 2:42: teaching, fellowship, Qurbono, prayer. Pray for vocations.
“Lord, I leave my nets; I will follow you.”
live: Pray each day this week for priests, religious and missionaries from your parish.
Invite one person to come with you to Holy Qurbono or a prayer meeting.
Keep silence and reverence in the church before and after Qurbono.
fathers: He admires the obedience of the fishermen: they did not delay or say “let us go home first”, but left everything at once, as Elisha left his oxen to follow Elijah (Homilies on Matthew 14).
On the burning bush: the fire that does not consume the bush foreshadows the Virgin who bore the Light without harm, and the mystery of God's presence (Life of Moses II).
magis: From the beginning Jesus associated his disciples with his own life; the Church is the communion with Jesus.
God reveals his name to Moses: “I AM”; the name expresses God's faithfulness.
Pope Francis on vocation: every life is a call to follow Christ and to serve.
saints: 14 Jan: St Devasahayam, martyr of Travancore. 15 Jan: Commemoration of Mary, Mother of God, for the seeds. 17 Jan: St Antony of Egypt.
2027-01-10.prayer: Lord Jesus, light of Galilee, you called fishermen to follow you and made them fishers of people. Call us again today: give us courage to leave our nets, reverence before your holiness, and joy in your Church. Raise up many vocations from our families. Amen.

quick: Jesus begins his mission by calling people.
God calls in the middle of ordinary work.
Leave the nets: following Christ needs a real decision.
2027-01-10.action: Invite one person to Holy Qurbono or a prayer meeting this week.
2027-01-10.question: What nets do I need to leave to follow Jesus more closely?
illus: Many priests and sisters from Kerala's coastal parishes grew up in fishing families. More than one says the call came while helping father mend the nets. The Gospel of the lake keeps happening in Kerala.

family.explain: Jesus walked by the lake and saw fishermen. He said: “Follow me!” They left their nets at once and went with him.
family.intention: We pray for vocations to the priesthood and religious life from our family and parish.
family.ask: Ask: “What is Jesus asking our family to do for him?”

catechism: Jesus calls disciples into communion with him.
Every person is called to love and serve.
kidsaint: Simon was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee. When Jesus called him, he left his boat and nets and followed him. Jesus made him the leader of the apostles. Lesson: say yes quickly when Jesus calls.
term: The season after the Baptism of the Lord, until the Great Fast. Its Sundays show Christ revealed in his ministry: calling disciples, teaching, and showing his glory.
termMore: At the burning bush Moses removed his sandals (Exodus 3:5). In Kerala many of the faithful still remove their footwear before entering the church.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, by the Sea of Galilee you called fishermen to follow you. Call us again as we gather, and give us courage to answer. Amen.
share: Follow me (Matthew 4:19). What does following Jesus ask of me now?
Moses took off his sandals on holy ground (Exodus 3:5). Do I approach God with reverence?
They devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, the breaking of bread and prayer (Acts 2:42). Which of these is weakest in my life?
interc: For vocations to priesthood and religious life.
For those who have left the Church, that they may hear Christ's call again.
For fishermen and all who work at sea.
For parish communities, that they may live like the first Christians.
For our group, that we may follow Christ faithfully.
pm.close: Father, your Son calls us to follow him. Give us generous hearts to leave what holds us back. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, last Wednesday we celebrated Denho, the Baptism of the Lord. Now Jesus begins his work. He goes to Galilee, a region of ordinary working people, and begins to preach: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.” And the first thing he does is call people.

He walks by the lake and sees fishermen at work: Simon and Andrew casting their nets, James and John mending theirs. He says: “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.” And immediately they left their nets and followed him. No delay, no long negotiation.

God always calls people at work. Moses was looking after sheep when he saw the burning bush and heard: “Remove your sandals, for the place where you stand is holy ground.” The ordinary place of his work became holy because God was there. Your kitchen, your office, your field can become holy ground too.

What are your nets? Your phone, your worries, your ambitions, your comforts? Jesus does not always ask us to leave our jobs, but he always asks us to put him first. And some of our young people he calls to leave everything for the priesthood or religious life. Let us pray for them, and let us answer him: “Lord, I will follow you.” Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus walked by a big lake and saw fishermen catching fish. He said: “Come, follow me! I will make you fishers of people!”
The fishermen left their nets straight away and went with Jesus. They became his friends, the apostles.
Jesus calls you too: to be his friend and bring others to him. Let's say: “Jesus, I will follow you!”

intro: After his Baptism Jesus begins his ministry in Galilee. Light dawns on a land in darkness, and ordinary fishermen hear a call that changes their lives. The same call reaches us.

sub: Jesus begins not in Jerusalem but in “Galilee of the Gentiles”, a mixed and despised region.
Isaiah's promise is fulfilled: a light for the nations.
Christ still begins where people sit in darkness: in our struggles and our neighbourhoods.
q: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.
The people who sat in darkness have seen a great light, and for those who sat in the region and shadow of death light has dawned.
points.apply: Pray for one person you know who is in darkness: illness, addiction, despair.

sub: God called Moses by name from the bush, and he answered: “Here I am.”
Jesus calls fishermen at their work: “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.”
They leave their nets “immediately”: a call delayed is often a call lost.
q: God called to him out of the bush, “Moses, Moses!” And he said, “Here I am.”
And he said to them, “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.” Immediately they left their nets and followed him.
points.apply: Ask: what “net” holds me back from following Jesus more closely? Leave it this week.

points.h: A community born of the call
sub: Those who answered became the first Church: teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayer.
God heals the brokenhearted and gathers his people.
Every call to follow Christ is also a call into his Church.
q: He heals the brokenhearted, and binds up their wounds.
They devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers.
points.apply: Join one parish activity (prayer group, catechism, charity) this month. Pray for vocations.

concl: The Light has come, the call has been given, and the community is gathered.
Let us answer like Moses, “Here I am”, and like the apostles, leave our nets to follow him.
2027-01-10.resolve: Pray daily this week for priestly and religious vocations from your parish.
